answer: Something I would genuinely like to be better at is managing my time more effectively. While I am fairly organised, I often find myself struggling to fit everything in, which leaves me feeling [[stretched]]. Between work, my IELTS preparation, family commitments and trying to keep up my reading, there never seem to be enough hours in the day. I am constantly [[juggling]] different things and rarely feel I am giving any of them my full attention. I want to improve because I believe better time management would reduce my stress and make me far more productive. To improve, I have started using planning tools and trying to prioritise my tasks more [[ruthlessly]], focusing on what truly matters. Every Friday evening I sit down and plan the week ahead, which already helps, because I start Saturday knowing exactly what needs doing first. I am also learning to say no to commitments that are not worth my time, which is surprisingly hard in a culture where refusing an invitation can seem rude. Honestly, I think time is our most precious resource, and using it wisely is one of the most valuable skills a person can develop. If I mastered it, I believe I could achieve far more while feeling less [[overwhelmed]]. It would give me more time for the things I actually enjoy, like evening walks and dinner with my family, which is the whole point. It is an ongoing effort, but even small improvements have already made a noticeable and [[tangible]] difference to my daily life.

followUps.q: Who in your family manages time best?
followUps.answer: My younger sister, without question. She plans her study schedule weeks in advance and actually sticks to it. I have started borrowing some of her methods, although I would never admit that to her.

followUps.q: Do you think people were better at managing time in the past?
followUps.answer: Perhaps they had fewer distractions. My father's generation didn't have phones constantly buzzing, so it was easier to focus. Today the challenge is less about time and more about attention.

note: Added his competing commitments (work, IELTS, family), weekly Friday planning and the cultural difficulty of saying no; plain 'precious' unmarked, added [[juggling]] and [[overwhelmed]].
